review: Fresh source and explicit-question-request procedural coverage challenge of benchmark-v5
scope: Original English Uprising 2023 v23-10-12 standard 2–4-player multiplayer with scoring standard two-player Rival; optional standard 20-contract CHOAM; relevant January 13 2025 general/Uprising FAQ. Excludes solo, Rival variants including Streamlined, six-player teams, cross-game expansions, later Bloodlines leaders.

material_findings.finding: The two zero-addition passes do not establish explicit-request saturation. Core phase priority, Reveal sequencing, starting deck/market state, acquisition-source rules, and human icon optionality/permanence remain unasked.
Ordinary matching access and pre-entry Plot resources need explicit tests; merely appearing in or following from a key is not question coverage.

Board-space effects are broadly represented, but complete access/Combat field coverage is overstated. Several fields are only unasked key background or absent. Amend existing questions rather than introduce cosmetically varied standalone space questions.
Standard two-player phase termination must honor remaining Rival Agent turns after both humans Reveal; Q19’s no-Reveal rule alone does not explicitly test how the phase reaches Combat.

new_questions.question: In a normal three- or four-player round, who takes the first Player Turn, how does turn order proceed after someone Reveals, and exactly when does Player Turns end? During Combat Intrigue, who has first priority, in which direction does priority proceed, and how many Combat Intrigues may an eligible player play before yielding?
new_questions.expected_answer: Player Turns starts with the First Player marker and proceeds clockwise one turn at a time. Skip anyone who has already Revealed; the phase ends when all players have Revealed. Combat Intrigue likewise begins with First Player and proceeds clockwise among players with at least one unit in the Conflict; each may play any number or pass.
new_questions.source_references: Main PDF pp8,14; run extraction lines397–459,813–826
new_questions.novelty: Turn priority, skipped players and phase termination are not requested by Q03/Q08/Q23; Q19 only asks the two-player Rival order. Any-number Combat permission is also unasked.

new_questions.question: What are the three steps of a Reveal turn, in order? Must the Reveal-box effects be resolved in card order, or may the player choose their order?
new_questions.expected_answer: Reveal Cards, Resolve Reveal Effects, Clean Up, in that order. Reveal all remaining hand cards first; resolve their Reveal effects in any chosen order; then clean up all played cards.
new_questions.source_references: Main PDF p12; run extraction lines714–748
new_questions.novelty: Q03 asks card eligibility/destination, Q13 purchase interleaving and Q71 strength timing; none requests the Reveal step sequence or effect-order freedom.

new_questions.question: Before the first round without CHOAM, how are each human starter deck, Intrigue deck, Imperium deck/Row and Reserve stacks prepared? Where do the human Combat marker, three Spies, Councilor and Control markers start?
new_questions.expected_answer: Each human shuffles their identical ten-card starting deck and puts it face down in their supply left of their Leader. Omit CHOAM-marked Imperium/Intrigue cards, shuffle the Intrigue and Imperium decks face down, deal five Imperium cards face up, and place Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks next to the Row. Human Combat marker starts at zero on the indicated initial side; three Spies, Councilor and Control markers start in their supply in clear view.
new_questions.source_references: Main PDF pp3–5; run extraction lines102–319, especially C1–C3/E/G3/G6
new_questions.novelty: Initial deck/market preparation and the remaining human component destinations are not requested by Q01/Q02/Q16/Q21/Q60/Q81. These establish playable initial state; not a numerical variant of an existing setup question.

new_questions.question: Which cards may you ordinarily acquire with Persuasion, where is each acquisition cost shown, and during which kind of your turn may you make those ordinary Persuasion purchases?
new_questions.expected_answer: During the player’s Reveal turn, acquire any available card from the five-card Imperium Row or Prepare the Way/The Spice Must Flow from the Reserve, paying the Persuasion cost printed at the top right. Ordinary Persuasion purchasing is a Reveal-turn procedure.
new_questions.source_references: Main PDF p13 Acquiring Cards and p20 Persuasion; run extraction lines775–806,1256–1259
new_questions.novelty: Q13 asks spending within Reveal, pooling, replacement and destination; it does not ask the legal purchase sources, printed price or whether an Agent turn permits ordinary purchases. Q34 only asks acquire-box/reshuffle rules.

new_questions.question: When a human receives a Spy placement icon or a Recall Spy icon, may the player decline the action even if a legal Spy/post exists? Does a Shield Wall destruction icon require destruction, and if destroyed can the Wall return in a later round?
new_questions.expected_answer: Ordinary Spy placement and ordinary Recall Spy are permissive: may place/recall. An unpaid optional recall cost gives no associated benefit; Intrigue costs/conditions still must be met to play that Intrigue. Shield Wall destruction is optional. Once removed, return it to the box; it is gone for the rest of the game.
new_questions.source_references: Main PDF pp10–11; FAQ pp3–4 optional effects/Shield Wall; run main lines577–585,646–665; FAQ lines217–228,304–306
new_questions.novelty: Q26 asks placement legality, Q73 asks recall resolution/destination and Q49 asks Sietch option outcomes, but none expressly requests these human icon optionality branches or Wall permanence. Q77 is Rival-specific and uses different mandatory automation.

new_questions.question: For an ordinary Agent turn, what must match between the played card and destination? You have a Spy connected to Shipping, but your played card has only a City Agent icon. Does the connected Spy itself let that card send an Agent to Shipping? What changes if the card actually has the Spy Agent icon?
new_questions.expected_answer: Ordinary access requires an Agent icon actually on the played card matching the destination’s access icon. A connected Spy alone does not give a City-only card access to Shipping. With an actual Spy Agent icon, the card may access a space connected to the player’s deployed Spy, without recalling that Spy for access; normal requirements and costs still apply.
new_questions.source_references: Main PDF pp9,11; run extraction lines487–500,675–677
new_questions.novelty: Matching access in Q04’s key is unasked background; Q06 explains a Spy Agent icon without requesting whether a deployed Spy creates one. This is a card-access permission distinction, not a changed destination-name example.

new_questions.question: You lack the resource for a destination’s entry cost. May you first play and resolve a Plot Intrigue during that Agent turn to obtain it, then pay entry and send the Agent? Contrast trying to use resources from the card played to send that Agent, or from the destination itself, to pay that same entry cost.
new_questions.expected_answer: Yes, if the Plot Intrigue is legally playable and provides the needed resource before placement/payment: Plot Intrigues may be played at any point during one of the player’s Agent turns. Pay the destination cost before resolving the destination or played Agent-card effects, so those later gains cannot fund their own entry.
new_questions.source_references: Main PDF pp7–9; run extraction lines390–394,418–430,504–519
new_questions.novelty: Consequential pre-entry Plot timing is not tested by Q04’s Agent-card/space prohibition or Q31’s broad card-type windows. It is not permission to pay a cost retroactively; the Plot actually resolves before entry.

new_questions.question: In standard two-player play, both humans take early Reveal turns while the Rival still has an Agent in its supply. Does Player Turns end immediately? What happens to the remaining Rival Agent turns, and does the Rival ever take a Reveal turn before Combat begins?
new_questions.expected_answer: Do not cancel the Rival’s remaining Agent turns. Skip the humans who Revealed and continue giving the Rival Agent turns while it has an Agent in its supply. Once both humans have Revealed and the Rival has no Agent remaining in supply, proceed to Combat. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
new_questions.source_references: Main PDF p8 Player Turns; Supplements PDF p4 Rival Agent Turns; run main lines409–429 and supplement lines226–235
new_questions.novelty: A required standard-Rival phase-termination exception: Main requires revealed humans to be skipped, while the supplement requires a Rival turn as long as an Agent remains and expressly prohibits Rival Reveal. Q19 requests Rival turn order/Reveal status, not termination after both humans Reveal early; Q82 is normal 3–4P. The result is a direct operational reconciliation of these source instructions.

explicit_question_request_assessment.method: An atom counts only when the actual question asks for it. A general effects request covers effects; it does not automatically request access icon, cost, Combat flag, priority or optionality. Existing key text is not coverage by itself.

independence_statement: Read only the authorized source packet/PDFs/unannotated supplement-p5 diagram, v5 questions/key/ledger, and v4 questions/key solely for preservation comparison excluding Q59. Did not read any summary version, reader output, grades, repair history or prior-review artifact; did not communicate with readers. The allowed ledger itself contains historical pass/scope entries. During the scan the parent supplied three source-only candidate questions (matching-card/Spy access, Plot pre-entry resources and Rival remaining-Agent phase termination), without reader facts; these were independently checked against source and actual question wording and are explicitly identified as Q87/Q88/Q89. The remaining findings were independently developed. Only coverage-review-v5.json was written; no bank, key or ledger was edited.
